about: What the review board (scripts/review-board.py, published as an artifact) shows besides the 64 shorts. The user, 2026-09-27: 'There's too many videos and styles and types spread all over the place for me to review. Create a nice artifact that's organized properly, with an easy way for me to check off that it's been reviewed with some comments.' Verdicts and comments are saved in the artifact's database, collection 'reviews', one document per item id.

lesson.title: The Wang Bi lesson
notes: The full lesson with the flight look and machine sounds, 3 min 41 s.
The camera comes in on 22 and goes down to line 5 once. It comes in again on 7.
The sweep and chatter play on each approach, the warble on the descent, the wind-down on the last answer. Music only on the end card.
One amber line at a time. The last page is the store copy's line: the conclusion is yours.

new.endcardsNote: The six tempos the first seven didn't cover. Each short now plays its tempo-independent card with no period. The other 51 wait for your verdict on these.

critiques.summary: Astra liked the hook, the look and the question. The terminal readout at 16-26 s is the main obstacle for newcomers.

points.text: "Grace says: small things only" is cryptic.
points.take: Agree. It is part of the "X says:" pattern, which 57 shorts use (see Open decisions).

points.text: Two takeaways: "Polish can't make big decisions" and "Plain is the best adornment".
The readout's text is small, the yin/yang/in/out/centre columns aren't explained, and L2 and L5 are both amber.
points.take: Agree on the two amber lines, which break our one-amber rule. The Wang Bi lesson explains the columns.

points.text: Show the app, or name the I Ching early.
points.take: Against our rules: shorts show no app screens.

critiques.summary: Astra found this more promising than Grace. The neon 蠱 is a real teaching device, but a viewer who can't read Chinese needs a key.

points.text: Explain the character as it builds: worms above, a vessel below.
points.take: Agree. Our own rule is English beside any Chinese. One gloss, such as "蠱: worms in a shut bowl", would do it. Labels on each part would be the kind of label you called cheesy.

points.text: "Rushed repairs don't hold" then "Found rot? Clean it out" reads like a quick fix.
points.take: Fair. The lesson could name the cause, for example "Found rot?\nClear out the cause."

points.text: Add one modern example instead of only historical plates.
points.take: Possible, but the plates are part of the series design. A big change.
Against the benchmark: the plain build stays.

critiques.summary: Astra's pick for a broad audience. "Steady care, not big gestures" is the strongest line, but the closing lesson drifts from the opening.

points.text: "Like fire, cling to what is right" brings in moral language after a lesson about steady care.
points.take: Agree. The Tuan's word 麗 (to cling) is about depending on what sustains you. "Fire clings\nto what feeds it." would close the loop.

points.text: "Keep it fed" after a burnout hook can read as "keep working".
points.take: Partly. The lesson change above would settle it.

points.text: The cattle plate has no visible link to fire.
points.take: Fair. The Judgment says to raise a cow, which stands for docility. Viewers aren't told that. Change the plate or caption it.

points.text: The hexagram changes colour at 14-19 s with no text.
points.take: That is the scene lesson, the lines acting out the fire. Whether it reads without a label is your call. Labels go against "no labels on bars".

points.text: Put "Six Lines — I Ching app" on the end card.
points.take: You already turned this down as cheesy.

decisions.title: The other 51 end cards
decisions.text: Render the remaining 51 tempo-independent cards (about 3.5 h in Blender, cards only), then re-render each short as it's reviewed.
decisions.after: Watch the six new end card shorts first.

decisions.title: The "X says:" opening
decisions.text: 57 of 64 shorts open their meaning with a line like "Decay says:" or "Grace says:". Astra found it unclear twice. Keep it, or rewrite it series-wide.

decisions.title: An English key for the characters
decisions.text: The 14 character lessons show a Chinese character with no English beside it. Add one short gloss per character, in the style of "蠱: worms in a shut bowl".

decisions.title: Lesson lines that close the loop
decisions.text: Astra's point on 18 and 30: the closing lesson should answer the opening hook. Check the other 62 lessons against their hooks.
